newsitem.title: USA: NYC Council sees bigger budget surplus in FY 1997.
newsitem.headline: NYC Council sees bigger budget surplus in FY 1997.

text.p: The New York City Council on Tuesday said that it expected the surplus at the end of the 1997 fiscal year to surpass the more than $300 million total projected by the city Comptroller Alan Hevesi.
Herbert Berman, chairman of the finance committee, said "We expect, in fact, that by year-end, given continued strong economic activity, that the projected surplus for fiscal 1997 will be larger."
The city's fiscal year ends on June 30.
Berman urged that any extra funds be used to deal with the $1.5 billion budget gap that the council projects for fiscal year 1998.
